summary.final_text:
The serial dilution is made in assay_plate wells A1–A4, 100 µL each, with PBS as the diluent.

| Well | Concentration | Made from |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | 2 mg/mL | 100 µL BSA stock |
| A2 | 1 mg/mL | 50 µL stock + 50 µL PBS |
| A3 | 0.5 mg/mL | 25 µL stock + 75 µL PBS |
| A4 | 0.25 mg/mL | 12.5 µL stock + 87.5 µL PBS |

The stock is already 2 mg/mL, so A1 is undiluted and each lower well is drawn directly from the stock with the matching PBS volume. This gives the same two-fold series, and each well has exactly 100 µL. I did not chain transfers from well to well, because that would leave A1–A3 short of 100 µL.

Each source change used a fresh tip. The reagent counts agree with the transfers: 187.5 µL of BSA stock and 212.5 µL of PBS were used. I did not read the plate, since no read was requested.

task_def.source: Two-fold serial dilution of a BSA standard, the usual way protein-assay standard curves are built (compare the diluted-standards table in the Thermo Scientific Pierce BCA Protein Assay user guide, MAN0011430, which also starts from 2 mg/mL BSA).
task_def.prompt: Make a two-fold serial dilution of the BSA standard across assay_plate wells A1 to A4, so that A1 is 2 mg/mL, A2 is 1 mg/mL, A3 is 0.5 mg/mL and A4 is 0.25 mg/mL, with 100 uL in each well. Dilute with PBS buffer.
